Configuring the scheduler

The scheduler reads its configuration from scheduler.toml at startup. Each job declares a cron expression, a command, and an optional timeout; jobs that exceed their timeout are terminated and reported as failed in the run log.

Concurrency is bounded per queue. When a queue is saturated, new runs wait in FIFO order rather than being dropped, so bursts of scheduled work are smoothed out over time without losing any runs.

To pause every job without editing the file, send SIGUSR1 to the scheduler process; send it again to resume. Pausing does not interrupt runs that are already in progress.

Logs rotate daily and are kept for fourteen days by default. Set retention_days to change this, or set it to zero to keep logs forever.

Metrics are exported in Prometheus format on the /metrics endpoint when metrics_listen is set, including queue depth, run duration histograms, and failure counts per job.

Every job also accepts an environment table whose keys and values are passed to the command unchanged, which keeps secrets out of the command line itself.

Jobs can depend on one another: a job with an after list only starts once every named job has finished successfully in the current window.

Finally, the scheduler exposes a dry-run mode that prints the next ten fire times of every job without running anything, useful when validating changes.

Related: Upgrading from 1.x

Version 2 renamed several configuration keys; see the upgrade guide for the full mapping between the old and new names and a migration script.
